foot_note: Summaries and facts verified against repo READMEs and GitHub APIs (2026-10-11)
insight: **Today's trending chart took a distinctly hardcore turn**: The top three spots belong to a reverse engineering MCP (morluto/rea, +25.6k in a single day), a PS5 porting toolkit (AnyPS5, +4.0k daily / +21.4k weekly), and an AI creative IDE (ArtCraft). Spots four through six feature diagramming capabilities for coding agents, a satellite data globe, and the original 1969 Apollo AGC source code—hardly any of them are 'yet another agent framework'; every single one is a specialized tool that dives deep into a specific vertical to get the job done right.

**'Deciphering closed-source software' has become the new battleground for agents**: REA consolidates Hopper, Ghidra, and IDA alongside Electron/asar and .NET static analysis into a single MCP, requiring every conclusion to be backed by concrete evidence and acknowledged limitations. AnyPS5 pushes even further—reincarnating executables via a relinker paired with in-house PRX libraries, strictly avoiding emulation or standalone runtimes, and already running a 2D platformer at a rock-solid 60 fps on a GTX 1050 Ti.

**Two generations of low-VRAM LLM execution share the stage**: The veteran AirLLM surged back onto the daily charts thanks to its newly introduced 'low-VRAM training' (fine-tuning 125B models on 6GB, and 27B on ~2GB). Meanwhile, colibri on the monthly leaderboard takes a completely different path: pure C, zero dependencies, and streaming MoE experts straight from disk. Both arrive at the exact same conclusion: the bottleneck isn't the algorithm—it's how you treat the memory hierarchy.

**This month's leaderboard remains a civil war among agent substrates**: Memory (hindsight +24.9k), orchestration and governance (paperclip +19.5k, ECC +22.4k), web-browsing capabilities (Agent-Reach +16.7k), and production-proven code review from Alibaba (open-code-review +23.9k) dominate six spots. Meanwhile, end-user creative tools claimed only two: VoiceStudio (+35.2k) and gods-eye-view (+27.9k)—solidify the infrastructure first, harvest vertical applications later.

rows.intro: A reverse engineering MCP server for coding agents: enables agents to understand an application without source code—tracing from UI behavior down to native binaries, and cloning an implementation along the way.
facts: An MCP server plus companion workflow skills: run `npx rea-agents setup` to register with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, etc. (with automatic config backups before changes), alongside a standalone `rea` CLI.

Broad target coverage: native binaries (decompiled pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references; hooks into locally installed Hopper / Ghidra / IDA), JavaScript and Electron apps (including `.asar`, fully static without a disassembler), .NET assemblies, and websites; also covers ELF layout diagnosis, WASM, and EVM bytecode.

All analysis runs locally; every finding requires concrete evidence and known limitations (as the README states: agents must provide code, references, and unknowns rather than unsubstantiated claims) for easy follow-ups and verification.

Requires Node.js 22.19+ / 24.11+ / 26+ and npm; MIT licensed, official site at rea.tools; created in April 2026, holds 102.7k stars via GitHub API, ranked #1 on today's trending with a +25.6k daily surge.

rows.intro: A toolchain that ports PS5 games to PC without emulation or separate runtime processes, directly recompiling PlayStation executables into native Linux/Windows binaries.
facts: Powered by a relinker that converts executables into native target formats, dynamically linking against reimplemented system PRX libraries (README: "No emulation or separate runtime process").
A shader recompiler outputs SPIR-V (validated via Spirv-Tools when building with `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS`), rendering natively via Vulkan.

Compatibility tracker at `docs/user/COMPATIBILITY.md`: verified titles like Dreaming Sarah (2D platformer) hit a stable 60 fps on a GTX 1050 Ti / i5-7500; unsupported states fail-fast by throwing `std::runtime_error` rather than silently degrading.

Out-of-the-box SDL gamepad support (sticks & triggers), with keyboard/mouse mapped via `anyps5-input.ini`; GPL-2.0, created August 2026; README explicitly clarifies it contains and requires no copyrighted firmware, keys, or proprietary libraries—intended solely for interoperability, research, and preservation.

rows.intro: A desktop creative suite dubbed the 'IDE for artists': compose scenes via 2D layering and 3D set staging before generating with models—turning AI generation from a gacha roll into a controllable, reproducible craft.
facts: Interactive image/video creation: 2D layer compositing, 3D depth compositing, character poses and camera presets, Character Identity Transfer (poseable mannequins driving character placement and stance), 3D kitbashing, background removal, masked inpainting, and image-to-video.

Built-in catalog of 62 models: 16 image models (Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, Seedream), 25 video models (Seedance, Kling, Veo, Sora, Vidu, MiniMax), plus audio/music, 3D meshes, and world/Gaussian splatting (Marble, TripoSplat); external providers like Grok, Midjourney, Sora, and World Labs are also supported.
Downloads: stable builds for Windows and macOS at getartcraft.com, latest releases on GitHub Releases, with Linux built from source; site includes a 2-minute demo video and Discord community.
Dual-licensed under MIT / Apache-2.0, written in Rust, created in March 2022 (with recent active revamping); currently sits at 17.8k stars via GitHub API.

rows.intro: An editorial-grade diagramming skill library for coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi: generates self-contained HTML+SVG diagrams across 38+ formats, ditching flimsy Mermaid charts and excessive drop shadows.
facts: Covers 38–39 diagram types: Sankey, fishbone, Wardley maps, Kanban, user journeys, deployment and dependency graphs, UML class diagrams, database schemas, and more (per README v2.5.10 release notes).
Decouples semantic schemas from layouts: patterns like queues, strategy tracking, and trust boundaries map to existing primitives, preventing unbounded type bloat.
Parses draw.io and Mermaid source files to redraw them at custom formats, dimensions, and detail levels; defaults to static HTML with optional accessible animations.
MIT licensed, created in April 2026, includes an online preview site; currently over 36k stars on GitHub API.

rows.intro: An in-browser spy satellite simulator powered entirely by real-world data: fuses flight transponders, maritime beacons, satellites in orbit, seismic stations, and public webcams onto a photorealistic 3D globe—running locally with auditable, extensible code.
facts: Created by bilawalsidhu from the viral YouTube series God's Eye View (formerly WorldView, 5M+ YouTube views, 25M+ across socials); hit #1 on GitHub Trending daily and weekly in August 2026, and #8 on Product Hunt (per README).

Two install paths: 1-click Pinokio desktop setup (Windows/macOS/Linux, requires Pinokio 8.2+) or via terminal / coding agents; tracks flights, military/satellites, earthquakes, public webcams, radio feeds, and rocket launches without accounts or API keys.

Photorealistic 3D terrain requires an optional Cesium ion token (free personal/non-commercial) or Google Maps API key via the in-app POWER UP panel; traffic is simulated along actual roads, while camera poses and rocket trajectories are rough approximations.

Features: cockpit view, 250km target roster, click-to-track targets, voice whiteboard, GLSL sensor shaders (CRT/NVG/FLIR/Noir), military HUD, scene director, and shareable tracking links; modular architecture with swappable data sources per layer; created June 2026, 31.8k stars on GitHub API.

rows.intro: The original assembly source code archive for the Apollo 11 Guidance Computer (AGC): a line-by-line digital transcription of the actual code that flew to the Moon in 1969, open for study and verification.
facts: Contains two flight programs: Comanche055 (Colossus 2A) for the Command Module and Luminary099 (Luminary 1A) for the Lunar Module, digitized in partnership between Virtual AGC and the MIT Museum; dedicated to the public domain.

Uses the yaYUL assembler, targeting the Virtual AGC project (www.ibiblio.org/apollo) for compilation and emulation; PRs correcting transcription discrepancies against original MIT Museum scans are welcomed.
Includes original documents such as `CONTRACT_AND_APPROVALS.agc`, showing NASA contract details and assembly revision timestamps from 1969-04-01 and 1969-07-14.

README translated into 40+ languages (including Simplified and Traditional Chinese); created in April 2014, currently at 74.2k stars via GitHub API, standing as one of GitHub's most enduring space archaeology projects.

rows.intro: An inference framework that runs massive LLMs on minimal VRAM: leverages layer-wise streaming and prefetching to offload weights to disk and RAM—running 70B models on a single 4GB GPU without quantization, distillation, or pruning.
facts: Official end-to-end benchmarks: Kimi K3 (2.8T) at 3.72GB on RTX 6000 Ada, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) at 5.95GB on RTX 4090, DeepSeek-V3 (671B) at ~12GB, and Qwen3.8-27B at 3.33GB on RTX 3090; K3 utilizes per-expert streaming to only load routed experts per token.

Supports training since September 2026: streams frozen weights layer-by-layer while keeping adapters resident in VRAM—training Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) within 6GB (RTX 3060 Ti), and Qwen3.8-27B in ~2GB at sequence length 512.

Minimal setup: `pip install airllm` and run inference just like standard Hugging Face transformers; `AutoModel` auto-detects architecture, with `layer_shards_saving_path` for caching layer shards; supports safetensors, 8-bit/4-bit quantization, and macOS on 70B models.

Supports Qwen, Llama 3.x/4, DeepSeek V2/V3, Phi, Gemma, ChatGLM, Baichuan, Mistral, and more; Apache-2.0, by Gavin Li, created June 2023, with 36.4k stars via GitHub API, making a resurgence on the daily trending chart.

rows.intro: The de facto standard deep learning framework: provides multidimensional tensors and dynamic computation graphs, making model definition, gradient computation, and GPU acceleration purely idiomatic Python.
facts: Core foundation: `autograd` reverse-mode automatic differentiation paired with dynamic computation graphs (define-by-run), seamless NumPy tensor interoperability, and unified APIs across training and inference.

Hardware backends cover CPU, NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and Apple Metal (MPS); accelerates execution via graph compiler `torch.compile`; scales out with DDP and FSDP distributed primitives, with TorchServe for deployment.

Rich ecosystem: torchvision (vision), torchaudio (audio), TorchScript / ONNX exports; serves as the underlying backbone for virtually all flagship LLMs and frameworks (transformers, vLLM, Unsloth, etc.).

Platform-specific installation via pytorch.org selector matrix (generating pip/conda commands like `pip3 install torch --index-url` for matching CUDA releases); created August 2016, 104.5k stars and 32.1k forks on GitHub API, charting on the daily trending list as an enduring infrastructure staple.

rows.intro: A toolchain for automatically porting PS5 games to PC: no emulators or separate runtime processes—it directly recompiles and relinks PlayStation executables into native Linux/Windows binaries.
facts: The core is a relinker that transforms executables into the target OS's native format, paired with custom-implemented system PRX libraries for dynamic linking (README quote: 'No emulation or separate runtime process').
The shader recompiler outputs SPIR-V (enabling `ANYPS5_ENABLE_SPIRV_TOOLS` validates output via Spirv-Tools at build time), with graphics running on Vulkan.

Compatibility list located at `docs/user/COMPATIBILITY.md`: verified titles include *Dreaming Sarah* (2D platformer) running at a stable 60 fps on a GTX 1050 Ti / i5-7500; unsupported states immediately terminate by throwing `std::runtime_error` rather than silently degrading.

Supports SDL gamepads (including thumbsticks and triggers) out of the box, with keyboard/mouse configurable via `anyps5-input.ini`; GPL-2.0, repository created in 2026-08; README explicitly states it neither includes nor requires copyrighted firmware, keys, or proprietary libraries, intended strictly for interoperability, research, and preservation.

rows.intro: A 'real engineer' skill pack by star TypeScript educator Matt Pocock: open-sourcing the exact `.agents` directory he uses daily for coding—small, hackable, composable, and without hijacking your workflow.
facts: The author explicitly differentiates this from heavy workflow frameworks like GSD/BMAD/Spec-Kit: does not wrest away control, keeping skills small, hackable, composable, and compatible with any model (README quote).
30-second setup via two options: Claude Code plugin (read-only hosted bundle that automatically updates with upstream) or pulled directly from the repo.
Accompanied by the aihero.dev skills newsletter, with ~60,000 subscribers per the README.
MIT license, created in 2026-02; 250k+ stars via GitHub API, ranked #1 on weekly trending with +13.4k stars this week.

rows.intro: A next-generation E2E testing framework for web and mobile: describe objectives in natural language, let the AI agent drive the app to that state, and verify results with locators and assertions within the same test case.
facts: Mixes natural language and assertions within the same test: e.g., `await agent.act('upgrade workspace to Pro')` followed by `agent.assert(...)` or `expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro')`.

Tests containing agent steps validated by subsequent assertions record actions and replay them directly on subsequent runs without calling models (re-engaging AI only when the app changes); tests without agent steps incur zero model cost.

Bring-your-own-model support: use your own subscription, API key, or local models; modular npm packages include `e2e` (SDK/CLI), `@e2e-dev/web` (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit via Playwright), `@e2e-dev/mobile` (iOS/Android emulators), and `@e2e-dev/github` (posts results as PR comments).

Install via `npx e2e init` (interactive setup for engine, web/mobile, and model provider); telemetry can be disabled with `npx e2e telemetry disable`; Apache-2.0, created in 2026-07, official site tester.army/e2e; 3,000+ stars via GitHub API (retrieved 2026-10).

rows.intro: HeyGen's open-source 'write HTML, render video' framework: deterministically renders HTML/CSS/media and seekable animations into MP4s—usable via local CLI or plugged into AI coding agents as skills, serving as an agentic video generation pipeline.
facts: Two usage modes: direct local CLI rendering, or install 20 skills via `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes` and prompt agents like 'Use /hyperframes to make a 10s product teaser'; supports Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, etc.

The entry skill is the router `/hyperframes`, with downstream workflows including `product-launch-video`, `faceless-explainer`, `pr-to-video`, `embedded-captions`, `talking-head-recut`, `motion-graphics`, `music-to-video`, `slideshow`, and `remotion-to-hyperframes`.
Deterministic rendering stack built on FFmpeg + Puppeteer, along with MCP topic tags; online Playground (hyperframes.dev) and Catalog (preset blocks) available.
Apache-2.0, requires Node.js >= 22, npm package name `hyperframes`; created in 2026-03, 49.6k stars via GitHub API.

rows.intro: A cross-session agent memory plugin: records everything an agent does in a session, compresses it via AI, and injects relevant context into future sessions—compatible with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode, and more.
facts: One-line installation: `npx claude-mem install` (or `/plugin install claude-mem` inside Claude Code, or via the `install.cmem.ai` script for OpenClaw); supports targeting hosts via `--ide opencode / grok-bot / antigravity / omp`.

Three memory provider options: officially hosted claude-mem observer (email-based browser login, no credit card required, 14-day free trial without consuming your own plan quotas), bring-your-own OpenRouter/Gemini keys, or use your Anthropic plan directly; `--provider host` allows local observation, and CI environments can skip authentication.

Note that the `claude-mem` package on npm is only an SDK/library; plugin installation must use `npx` or `/plugin`, otherwise plugin hooks and worker services will not be registered (stated explicitly in the README).

Tech stack includes ChromaDB for vector retrieval and `claude-agent-sdk` (from repo topics); Apache-2.0, created in 2025-08, official site claude-mem.ai; 96k+ stars via GitHub API (retrieved 2026-10).

rows.intro: A plugin equipping coding agents with 'CAD superpowers': generate STEP, GLB, STL, and 3MF 3D models locally from a single prompt, complete with DFM checks, engineering drawings, and manufacturing service integrations.
facts: Core pipeline: local 3D model generation → Design for Manufacturability (DFM) checks → engineering drawings → integration with mainstream 3D printing, sheet metal, and CNC machining services (README quote).

Install with a single prompt: 'Install text-to-cad from https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad', and it self-installs; Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, and Grok have dedicated official plugin/extension installation methods; the CAD engine runs via `uv` (`cadgen mcp` local service + built-in viewer).

Tech stack: Python 3.11+ / Node 20+, geometry kernel build123d 0.11 + Open CASCADE 7.9, PyPI package name `cadgen`; models appear as interactive rotatable viewer cards in chat, while CLI-based hosts output browser CAD Viewer links.

Anonymously reports usage and crash metrics by default (randomized ID, excludes files, paths, or prompts), toggleable off via `uvx cadgen telemetry off`; MIT license, official site texttocad.dev; created in 2026-04, 19.2k stars via GitHub API.

rows.intro: A 'rig' for multi-agent teams: define your agent roster in YAML and assemble Claude Code and Codex into a unified rig with a single command to manage them as one coherent system.
facts: Positioned simply: a harness wraps models; a rig wraps your harnesses. It transforms scattered terminal sessions into a standing team with designated roles, shared context, and task claiming—you communicate goals only with the lead agent, which coordinates specialized team members.
Requirements: Node.js 22 or 24 + tmux, macOS/Linux only (native Windows unsupported, WSL2 untested); install via `npm install -g @openrig/cli`; preview modifications first with `rig setup --dry-run`.

Reuses existing accounts: use Claude Code, Codex, or both without additional subscriptions; prompts once before launch for permission to execute rig commands without recurring confirmations (revocable), writing provider hooks and workspace trust settings.

Author mvschwarz uses it to run 'AI civilization' experiments; features a companion TUI visualization (team graph → agent seating chart → seat details including runtime, model, context, and status); Apache-2.0, created in 2026-04, official site openrig.dev; ~5,000 stars via GitHub API (retrieved 2026-10).

rows.intro: Cursor's official plugin specification and marketplace repository: defines agent plugin architecture (directory layout, manifests, skills, and MCP configs) while providing a full catalog of official and third-party plugins to reference.
facts: Repository root houses `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` listing all plugins; each plugin resides in a standalone directory with its own `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, structured into `skills/` (containing `SKILL.md` with frontmatter), `rules/` (`.mdc`), and `mcp.json`.

Lists 91 plugins total, 73 of which are `third_party` integrations: Semrush, Ahrefs, GoDaddy, Todoist, Calendly, Smartsheet, Teams, SharePoint, BigQuery, plus financial/trading services like Webull, Interactive Brokers, Robinhood, Coinbase, eToro, QuickBooks, Xero, Square, and more.

Includes Cursor's first-party workflow plugins: Thermos (branch-level security/correctness deep auditing + parallel subagents + optional PR merge flows), Ralph Loop (Ralph Wiggum-style iterative feedback loop), cursor-team-kit (CI, reviews, releases, and local automation), pr-review-canvas, docs-canvas, cursor-sdk, create-plugin, etc.
MIT license, maintained by Cursor's official GitHub organization, repository created in 2026-01 with frequent updates; 10.9k stars via GitHub API.

rows.intro: A fully local, open-source ElevenLabs alternative: an all-in-one suite for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, transcription, and audiobook generation—requiring no accounts, API keys, subscriptions, or usage-based billing.
facts: Features 16 TTS engines and 11 ASR engines across 646 cataloged languages (actual coverage and quality depend on the chosen engine); engines can be hot-swapped in the model catalog or via Ctrl/Cmd+E.

Cross-platform support covers macOS 13.3+ (Apple Silicon), Windows 10/11 x64, and Linux x86_64 (requires glibc 2.39+), plus a Docker image (linux/amd64) and a zero-install Colab demo; hardware backends include CUDA, Apple MPS/MLX, Linux ROCm, or pure CPU, with support for offloading to remote workers.

Beyond the desktop app, it exposes local REST/SSE/WebSocket interfaces, an OpenAI-compatible audio API, and an MCP server; all voice models, projects, settings, and outputs remain strictly on-device by default.

Formerly OmniVoice-Studio, licensed under AGPL-3.0; the README notes an ongoing Electron rewrite and active beta status, recommending latest Releases for production work; created in 2026-04, currently at 26.7k stars via the GitHub API.

rows.intro: An in-browser "spy satellite simulator" powered entirely by real data: aggregates flight transponders, maritime vessels, orbiting satellites, seismic stations, and public webcams onto a photorealistic 3D globe—runs locally, fully auditable, and extensible.
facts: Created by bilawalsidhu from the viral YouTube series God's Eye View (formerly WorldView; 5M+ YouTube views, 25M+ across social media); hit #1 on GitHub Trending Daily and Weekly in 2026-08, and #8 Product of the Day on Product Hunt (per the README).

Two setup paths: 1-click install via the Pinokio desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux, requires Pinokio 8.2+) or local run via terminal/coding agents; layers for flights, military/satellites, earthquakes, public webcams, radio, and rocket launches work out of the box with no accounts or API keys required.

Photorealistic 3D terrain requires your own Cesium ion token (personal, non-commercial) or Google Maps API key, configured in the in-app POWER UP panel; road traffic is simulated along actual transit networks, while camera poses and rocket trajectories are rough approximations.

Features: cockpit POV, 250km target manifests, click-to-track on any entity, voice whiteboard, GLSL sensor filters (CRT/NVG/FLIR/Noir), military HUD, scene director, and shareable tracking links; each layer is an isolated module with swappable data sources; created in 2026-06, currently at 31.8k stars via the GitHub API.

rows.intro: A long-term memory system for AI agents: goes beyond logging chat histories to help agents genuinely "learn" from experience—claims state-of-the-art results on the LongMemEval long-term memory benchmark.
facts: Built by Vectorize under the MIT license; website: hindsight.vectorize.io, paper: arXiv:2512.12818; created in 2025-10, currently at 37.2k stars via the GitHub API, ranking #1 on both daily and weekly trending.

The README highlights that benchmark results were independently reproduced by Virginia Tech's Sanghani Center for AI and Data Analytics and The Washington Post (contrasting with self-reported vendor scores), with accuracy, latency, and cost continuously updated at benchmarks.hindsight.vectorize.io.

Deployment: single-command Docker launch (API on 8888, UI on 9999, volume-persisted data), alongside pip/npm clients and an embedded Python mode (no standalone server required); supports 25+ LLM providers including local runtimes (ollama/lmstudio/llamacpp), any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and direct hooks into ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot subscriptions.

Core primitives center on retain, recall, and reflect operations paired with a memory bank; integrates via a 2-line LLM wrapper into existing agents, or via an MCP server with coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor (including docs skills installed via `npx skills add`).

rows.intro: Alibaba has open-sourced its internal AI code review assistant battle-tested over two years: combines a deterministic pipeline with tool-augmented LLM agents to deliver line-precise reviews on Git diffs; officially reported to serve tens of thousands of internal engineers and detect millions of defects.
facts: The agent analyzes beyond diffs: inspects full files, searches the codebase, and cross-references co-modified files in the same changeset for contextual depth; built-in multilingual rule sets cover NPEs, thread safety, XSS, and SQL injection, with model compatibility across OpenAI and Anthropic.

Install via `npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review` to access the `ocr` CLI; configure models via `ocr config provider` and `ocr config model` (with interactive connectivity checks), then run `ocr review` for workspace diffs, `--from`/`--to` for branch ranges, `--commit` for single commits, and `ocr scan` for full-repo scans; supports `--format json` output and session resumption.

Features a delegation mode where OCR solely handles file selection and rule parsing, allowing the host coding agent to run reviews without separate LLM configuration; provides plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Kimi Code, as well as an MCP server.

Requires Git ≥ 2.41; written in Go under Apache-2.0, holds an OpenSSF Best Practices Gold badge; website: open-codereview.ai; created in 2026-05, currently at 41.9k stars via the GitHub API, ranking #6 this week and #5 this month.

rows.intro: A performance-optimizing harness system for coding agents: combines skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development to help Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and others run faster and more reliably.
facts: Hosted at ecc.tools; self-described in the README as an agent harness operating system spanning five core pillars: skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first workflows.
Explicitly supports leading coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor (verbatim from the official description).
Documentation is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, and more; MIT licensed; created in 2026-01.
Over 250k stars recorded via the GitHub API; listed on both the daily and weekly trending leaderboards.

rows.intro: An open-source multi-agent team management application: breaks down business objectives into discrete goals, assigns roles, budgets, and permissions to different agents, and tracks progress and costs in a task-manager-style dashboard—as the project puts it: "If OpenClaw is an employee, Paperclip is the company."
facts: Architected as a Node.js backend with a React UI; operates in three fixed steps: define goals (e.g., "Scale a product to $1M MRR") -> assemble the team (CEO/CTO/Engineering/Design/Marketing, using any bot or provider) -> approve and run, with options to intervene or adjust budgets directly from the dashboard.
Integrates with OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Bash, and HTTP (in the README's words: anything wakeable via heartbeat can be "hired").

Built on "Four Pillars": Org Chart, Budget & Governance, Goal Alignment, and Agent Coordination; designed for running 20+ agent terminals simultaneously for unattended 24/7 execution with full auditability, complete with mobile management support.
MIT licensed; website: paperclip.ing, docs: docs.paperclip.ing; created in 2026-03, currently at 89.7k stars via the GitHub API, ranked #3 on the daily and #5 on the weekly leaderboard.

rows.intro: A CLI + Skill package giving AI agents instant web-browsing capabilities: enables Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, and others to read and search Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and Xiaohongshu with zero API fees.
facts: Comprises a CLI tool and a `SKILL.md` file—no manual commands to memorize, as the agent invokes them autonomously; features primary/fallback multi-backend routing per platform with automated failover (e.g., auto-switching from yt-dlp to bili-cli after Bilibili's 2026-06 anti-scraping crackdown, requiring zero user intervention).

All tools are open source and APIs are free, with the only potential expense being an overseas proxy server (~$1/mo), free on local machines; supports web-wide semantic search (via MCP), Xiaohongshu, and Xiaoyuzhou podcast transcription (Whisper).

Platforms requiring authentication demand explicit user authorization: Twitter/X strictly accepts manual exports from Cookie-Editor without automated login or cookie injection; OpenClaw users must enable `exec` permissions to allow the agent to run commands like `pip install`.

MIT licensed, requires Python 3.10+; README available in Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean; official badge shows a #1 ranking on GitHub Trending Daily, currently at 90k+ stars via the GitHub API (fetched 2026-10).

rows.intro: A pure C, zero-dependency inference engine designed to run massive models on constrained hardware: unifies NVMe, system RAM, and VRAM into a tiered memory hierarchy, enabling frontier MoE models (744B to 2.8T parameters) to run on consumer-grade and heterogeneous hardware by streaming expert weights directly from disk.
facts: Supports 9 model families: GLM-5.2/5.3 (744B), GLM-5.3-Flash (321B, multimodal), Inkling (975B), Kimi K3 (2.8T), DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B) and V4.1 Flash (552B, multimodal), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3.6 (35B-A3B), and OLMoE (7B)—each implemented in a single C file, sharing unified `coli chat`, `coli serve`, and `coli web` entrypoints.

Benchmark metrics (README screenshot): GLM-5.2 744B int4 achieves 4 tok/s with a TTFT of 1.6s on 6× RTX 5090 with zero disk reads (all experts resident in memory); the web dashboard displays VRAM/RAM/disk tier breakdowns and turn latency profiles, with Brain/Atlas pages visualizing 19,456 experts by memory tier and observed routing affinity.

Clear design philosophy: no speed SLA, but hard semantic guarantees—default policy never silently alters precision or routing semantics, trading throughput for capacity rather than swapping models; ensures correctness via token-exact forward validation and 57× compressed MLA KV cache.

Apache-2.0 licensed; website: justvugg.github.io/colibri; README available in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Italian; created in 2026-07, currently at 29.7k stars via the GitHub API.
